description: Environmental justice is a social movement that addresses injustice when poor or marginalized communities are harmed by hazardous waste, resource extraction, and other land uses from which they do not benefit. The movement has generated hundreds of studies showing that exposure to environmental harm is inequitably distributed. It encompasses various subtopics including sustainability, human rights, ecological ethics, climate equity, and community engagement.

key_takeaways: Environmental justice addresses the disproportionate impacts of environmental harm on marginalized communities
Sustainability, human rights, ecological ethics, climate equity, and community engagement are key concepts in environmental justice
The movement has its roots in the 1960s Civil Rights Movement and has evolved to address climate change and sustainability
real_world_impact: Environmental justice has significant real-world implications, from the creation of urban green spaces to the implementation of climate equity principles in international agreements like the Paris Agreement. The movement has also led to increased community engagement and recognition of the disproportionate impacts of natural disasters on marginalized communities. As the world continues to grapple with the challenges of climate change and sustainability, environmental justice will play a crucial role in ensuring that the transition to a more sustainable and equitable economy is just and fair for all.
